stories.body: The United States said it struck three Iran-linked oil tankers after Iranian missile attacks targeted a US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer; US Central Command said the warships evaded the attacks and no American personnel were hurt. Two tankers were described as permanently disabled and a third, reportedly empty, as destroyed, including strikes near Kharg Island and in the Gulf of Oman. Iranian state media said Iran retaliated by targeting three US-affiliated vessels and three oil tankers using what it called unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz. The exchange further escalates a conflict that resumed about a week ago after a month of relative calm, while the strategically vital strait has been effectively closed since the war began.
stories.headline: US and Iran exchange attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner headed to Kyiv after a three-hour meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, where the White House said they discussed substantive plans for next steps toward ending the war. Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov described the talks as constructive and frank, while saying Russia remained confident it could achieve its military objectives in eastern Ukraine. Details of any proposal have not been released, and no breakthrough was announced. The visit will be the negotiators' first trip to Kyiv, where they are expected to meet President Volodymyr Zelenskyy; Russia and Ukraine have separately agreed to pause strikes on each other's capitals for three days during the diplomatic effort.
stories.headline: US envoys travel to Kyiv after talks with Putin on ending the Ukraine war

stories.body: Voters in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt are choosing a new regional parliament in an election that could give the far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD, its first state-level hold on power in postwar Germany. Polls put the party near 40%, ahead of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats, and suggested it could win an outright majority if smaller parties fail to clear the threshold for parliament. AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund has presented the vote as a step toward national power in 2029, while the party's opponents warn of the implications of its hardline positions on migration, LGBT rights, education and relations with Russia. If it falls short of a majority, other parties' refusal to cooperate with the AfD could leave it unable to form a government.
stories.headline: Germany votes in Saxony-Anhalt as the far-right AfD seeks a historic state victory

stories.body: Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon killed four people, including two women, according to Lebanon's health ministry. Israel's military said the strikes responded to an alleged Hezbollah drone launch aimed at troops in the Israeli-occupied security zone in southern Lebanon. The deaths come amid a wider escalation in which Lebanese authorities say Israeli attacks since October 2023 have killed more than 8,900 people and wounded nearly 30,600, though those broader figures could not be independently verified in the reports. Lebanon's health ministry has also recorded repeated attacks on ambulance crews and healthcare workers.
stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill four people in Lebanon after an alleged Hezbollah drone launch

stories.body: Rescuers in Nepal found additional survivors as searches continued nearly two weeks after catastrophic floods triggered by a glacial and rock collapse. A Chinese worker was pulled from a 225-metre tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, while a 64-year-old Nepali woman was rescued from a mud-buried home in Nuwakot; other workers had also been recovered from tunnels. Rescue teams are concentrating on damaged hydropower projects, where hundreds of workers are believed missing or trapped. Nepal's disaster agency has reported at least 1,375 deaths and more than 5,000 people missing, while families of unidentified victims are increasingly conducting symbolic funeral rites as the scale of the disaster overwhelms recovery and identification efforts.
stories.headline: Nepal flood rescuers find more survivors as searches enter their twelfth day

stories.body: Volcanic ash from an eruption of Anak Krakatau forced Indonesia's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport near Jakarta to suspend flight operations, disrupting hundreds of flights and affecting more than 22,000 passengers. Authorities said the eruption, which began late Friday and continued with further activity on Sunday, sent ash into airspace over the capital despite the volcano being more than 150 kilometres away. Flights on domestic and international routes, including connections to Singapore, Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur, were affected as officials extended the closure while monitoring conditions. Authorities said there was no tsunami warning, but urged people in affected areas to guard against ash-related respiratory, eye and skin risks.
stories.headline: Anak Krakatau eruption suspends flights at Indonesia's main airport

stories.body: An Egyptian criminal court sentenced television presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other defendants to death by hanging after finding them guilty of operating a gang that imported materials to manufacture and traffic narcotics. Authorities said they seized more than 750 kilograms of narcotics and raw materials, along with firearms and ammunition, and found apartments allegedly used as drug laboratories. Khalifa, known for the crime-focused television program Mission Impossible, denies the accusations and plans to appeal. Nine co-defendants received life sentences and seven were acquitted; the death verdict was confirmed after the legally required consultation with Egypt's grand mufti.
stories.headline: Egyptian television presenter among 12 sentenced to death in a drugs case

stories.body: A former Immigration and Customs Enforcement official warned in an August 2025 whistleblower complaint that the agency was making final job offers to new officers before completing basic background checks, including fingerprinting, identity verification and credit checks. The complaint came as ICE expanded staffing for President Donald Trump's mass-deportation campaign and background-check backlogs mounted. The official, formerly a unit chief in ICE's Office of Professional Responsibility, said the practice violated federal rules and created risks of infiltration, insider compromise and misconduct. The complaint was obtained by the Associated Press through the retired official's lawyer after being first reported by The New York Times.
stories.headline: ICE hiring standards face scrutiny as whistleblower alleges unprecedented vetting cuts

stories.body: The US Supreme Court ruled that political parties are entitled to discounted television advertising rates when they coordinate campaign spending with candidates. The decision is expected to benefit party organizations, particularly Republicans, by allowing coordinated political advertisements to qualify for the lower rates available to candidates.
stories.headline: Supreme Court says political parties can receive discounted television ad rates for coordinated spending

stories.body: The Justice Department has sued the Kansas City, Kansas, school district over policies that allow students to use preferred names and pronouns and assess requests not to involve parents on a case-by-case basis. The Trump administration argues that the district's approach violates the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act by withholding information about a student's gender transition from parents. The district, which serves more than 20,000 students, disputes that it is out of compliance with federal law. It is the administration's first lawsuit using FERPA to assert what it describes as parents' right to know about a child's gender transition.
stories.headline: Justice Department sues Kansas school district over transgender-student policies

stories.body: Spain's transport ministry has taken control of part of Ceuta's port to install temporary tents for roughly 1,000 migrants, overriding opposition from the port authority, the city government and local business groups. The government invoked emergency powers to authorize use of about 16,000 square metres in the port after the authority argued that accommodation there was incompatible with normal operations and port law. Officials say the tents will provide temporary shelter and services while migration cases are processed. The decision follows public opposition to using sports halls and reflects mounting pressure on Ceuta's accommodation system after a large influx of migrants.
stories.headline: Spain takes control of Ceuta's port to house migrants amid a deepening accommodation crisis

stories.body: Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres called for political consensus to resolve Ceuta's migration crisis quickly and prevent it from becoming permanent. He said the temporary port accommodation is intended to allow authorities to identify migrants, process their cases and determine whether they should be returned or may seek asylum. The government says the facilities had been included in an emergency decree approved with local representation, but the port authority later objected. Ministers are also concerned that sharp rhetoric from opposition parties and unrest at demonstrations could intensify social tensions, as criticism of the government's handling of the crisis spreads across the political spectrum.
stories.headline: Spanish government seeks consensus to prevent the Ceuta migration crisis from becoming entrenched

stories.body: Spain's government says it will rely on its own and European investigations into the causes of the mass migrant arrivals in Ceuta, despite Morocco's announcement that it is conducting an inquiry. Officials in Madrid point to signs including alleged inaction by Moroccan authorities, but say any major diplomatic shift must be backed by clear evidence. The government is preparing to ask Brussels to review cooperation agreements with Rabat and seek stronger border-control guarantees if investigations support concerns about Moroccan responsibility. The dispute has added to pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, with opposition parties and coalition partners urging a tougher stance.
stories.headline: Spain presses Morocco over Ceuta migration surge while weighing an EU response

stories.body: Begoña Gómez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, has again asked to be acquitted in a case alleging influence peddling and embezzlement connected to an extraordinary chair she helped establish and co-direct at the Complutense University of Madrid. Her new lawyer argues that she did not use her position as the prime minister's wife to influence university officials, did not obtain financial benefit and did not appropriate a technological platform linked to the project. The defense says the university suffered no financial loss and that the chair followed established procedures. A popular prosecution group is seeking a 13-year prison sentence, while Gómez's lawyers say the allegations are untrue and do not constitute a crime.
stories.headline: Begoña Gómez again seeks acquittal in influence-peddling and embezzlement case

stories.body: Barcelona recorded another exceptional September temperature as the Fabra Observatory reached 35.5°C, its fourth consecutive daily record for the month and more than two degrees above its previous longstanding September record from 1983. The heat followed what meteorological reports described as the warmest September night on record across Catalonia, with a minimum of 27.1°C at the Fabra Observatory and even higher overnight readings elsewhere. Meteorological services said the intense heat had also produced records throughout Catalonia, including 42.5°C at Vinebre, and civil-protection authorities kept heat alerts in place through the weekend before an expected gradual easing from Monday.
stories.headline: Barcelona records another historic September heat mark, reaching 35.5°C

stories.body: Catalonia's rural agents raised the Alfa wildfire plan to its highest level in 106 municipalities across 17 counties, citing extreme fire danger driven by very high temperatures, low humidity, light winds and dry vegetation. Access to natural areas in the Baronia de Rialb and Serra de Mont-roig in La Noguera was restricted, while a very high-risk alert was activated in hundreds more municipalities. Outdoor activities that could start a forest fire remain prohibited. Civil-protection authorities also maintained an intense-heat warning for Sunday, especially in southern Catalonia.
stories.headline: Extreme wildfire risk prompts closures of natural areas in 17 Catalan counties

stories.body: The annual cost of schooling in Catalonia has risen to an estimated €2,994 per pupil, making it Spain's second-most expensive autonomous community after Madrid, according to the OCU consumer organization. Its survey puts the nationwide average at €2,484 per child, but costs vary sharply by school type: about €1,294 at public schools, €3,450 at subsidized private schools and €8,761 at private schools. Catalan family groups point to the higher share of subsidized and private education as a major factor and are calling for free school meals and excursions and limits on textbook costs. Separate estimates put the immediate September outlay for public-school families at about €735.
stories.headline: School costs in Catalonia rise to nearly €3,000 per pupil annually, consumer group says

stories.body: A proposed urban plan for the future Clínic-UB Health Campus would transform the Diagonal gateway into a new metropolitan district spanning Barcelona, Esplugues de Llobregat and L'Hospitalet de Llobregat. The project would grow to 500,000 square metres, including major health and research facilities, a new Hospital Clínic, medical and pharmacy faculties, and complementary services. It also reserves land for up to 1,125 homes, at least half officially protected, with most planned in L'Hospitalet. Backed by an estimated €1.7 billion investment, the campus is scheduled to open in 2035 alongside a new L3 metro station, with an international architecture competition expected in the coming weeks.
stories.headline: Barcelona plans a new 1,000-home neighborhood and the Clínic-UB campus at the Diagonal entrance
